AddMessagePayload.description:
Body of `POST /tenant/conversations/{id}/messages`.  `kind` is the
sender role; the handler resolves the membership id and audit metadata
from the authenticated principal.

AddMessageResponse.description:
Response of `POST /tenant/conversations/{id}/messages`: the inserted
message plus the refreshed conversation status reference.

scope.description:
Distinguishes the effective scope of the configuration: `platform_default`
when the response is the platform-wide default, or `tenant` when the
tenant has its own override (or — for a tenant GET — is being returned
with the platform fallback applied).

Assignee.description: Staff assignee reference embedded in conversation and message responses.

ChannelIdentifierInput.description:
Raw channel-identifier entry as supplied on the wire.  The DB normalizes
the value (trim + lowercase) but format checks happen before the round
trip so the UI gets a clean `422 details[]` per channel.

CitationView.description:
A citation linking an AI message to a knowledge-base passage at the
time the reply was generated.  Snapshotted so the citation remains
readable even if the source item is later deleted or updated.

ConfidenceView.description:
Deterministic confidence metadata attached to AI messages.
Band is derived server-side using a local 3-line function (see
`confidence_band`) — intentionally duplicated from `ai::confidence`
to avoid a circular crate dependency.

code.description: A six-digit code from the authenticator app.

Conversation.description:
Inbox-row projection of a conversation, returned by
`GET /tenant/conversations`.

ConversationDetail.description:
Full conversation detail returned by the create / update / get handlers.

`participants` lists every party on the conversation (the customer plus
any staff assignees).  Optional fields follow the wire's nullable
semantics; `assignee` and `last_message` are both optional+nullable.

ConversationDetailResponse.description:
`POST /tenant/conversations`, `PATCH /tenant/conversations/{id}` and the
composite `GET /tenant/conversations/{id}` all return the same
`{data: ConversationDetail}` shape — the escalation context merged by
the server-side handler is documented separately on the composite
endpoint (T019).

ConversationStatus.description:
Conversation lifecycle status.

Variants serialize to their snake_case wire names (`open`, `pending`,
`resolved`, `closed`) via the explicit serde rename; the OpenAPI schema
surfaces the same names so the documented vocabulary matches the wire
format (FR-006 / data-model.md).

ConversationStatusRef.description:
Updated conversation status + activity timestamp returned alongside an
inserted message.

ConversationSummary.description:
Per-conversation summary returned by the customer-profile history
endpoint.  A narrower projection than `model::Conversation`: no
`last_message` or assignee, since the dashboard only needs the metadata
to render the list.

CreateConversationPayload.description:
Body of `POST /tenant/conversations`.  Creates a conversation with the
first message (always a `reply` per FR-007).

CreateCustomerPayload.description:
Body of `POST /tenant/customers`.  Mirrors the contract in
`specs/012-customer-profiles/contracts/rest-api.md`.

CreateTenantRequest.description:
`CreateTenantRequest` — body for `POST /api/v1/platform/tenants`.

`name` and `slug` are typed as `Option<String>` (not `String`) so that a
missing field still deserializes successfully and the handler can return a
422 with a precise per-field error.  Bad JSON syntax or unknown fields
still fall through to `ApiJson`'s 400, which is the desired split.

`plan` uses `Option<Option<String>>` with the optional-nullable-string
deserializer (T101) so the handler can distinguish:
  * Field absent → `None` → default to "trial".
  * Explicit JSON `null` → `Some(None)` → 422.
  * Supplied value → `Some(Some(s))` → validate.

api_key.description:
Provider API key. Accepted on input only; never echoed back in any
response. The OpenAPI schema marks this field as `writeOnly`.

EnrolRequest.description:
Starting enrolment proves the account owner is present: it needs the current password, so a
stolen session alone cannot add an attacker's authenticator.

password.description: The signed-in user's current password. Never echoed back.

otpauthUri.description: The `otpauth://` URI a QR code carries. Shown once, here.

secret.description: The secret as base32, to type into an authenticator app. Shown once, here.

HistoryResponse.description:
`GET /tenant/customers/{id}/conversations` response envelope
(`{data, pagination}`).  Doc-only — the handler builds the body inline
with `Json(HistoryResponse { ... })`.

LastMessagePreview.description: Preview snippet of the most recent message on a conversation.

email.description: Email address of the user attempting to authenticate.

password.description:
Plain-text password supplied by the caller. Never echoed back in any
response; the OpenAPI schema marks this field as `writeOnly`.

MemberSkillsResponse.description:
`PUT /tenant/members/{membershipId}/skills` response envelope
(`{data}` — the updated skill list).

Message.description:
One message in a conversation, returned by the timeline endpoint and
embedded in `AddMessageResponse`.

MessageKind.description:
Message kind — the sender role that produced a given message row.

Variants serialize to their snake_case wire names (`customer`, `reply`,
`note`) so the documented vocabulary matches the wire format
(FR-006 / data-model.md).

MfaRequiredResponse.description: The body of the response to a password step that needs a second factor.

Participant.description:
One party in a conversation: either the customer (and a `type` of
`customer` with `id` set) or a staff assignee (and a `type` of
`assignee` with `membership_id` and `active` set).  The `type` field is
renamed via serde to match the wire shape; the OpenAPI schema surfaces
the same field name.

PatchConversationPayload.description:
Body of `PATCH /tenant/conversations/{id}`.  At least one of `status`
or `assigned_membership_id` MUST be supplied (the handler returns 422
otherwise).  `assigned_membership_id` is tri-state on the wire:

  * field absent            → leave assignment unchanged.
  * field = `null`          → unassign.
  * field = `uuid`          → assign to that membership.

PlatformTenantDetail.description: `PlatformTenantDetail` — full record returned by create/get/update handlers

Principal.description: Authenticated user principal resolved from the request context.

PublicWidgetConfigResponse.description:
`{ "data": PublicWidgetConfigDto }`, the envelope the public widget contract specifies
(specs/023-website-chat-widget/contracts/public-widget-api.md).

recoveryCodes.description: Ten single-use codes. Shown once, here; only their hashes are kept.

SessionResponse.description: `{ "data": SessionResponseDto }`, the envelope the public widget contract specifies.

displayName.description: The signing-up user's display name. 1-200 characters.

email.description: Email address for the new account.

password.description:
Plain-text password supplied by the caller. Never echoed back in any
response; the OpenAPI schema marks this field as `writeOnly`.

workspaceName.description: Name for the new workspace (tenant). 1-200 characters.

TenantFeedbackDto.description:
Feedback left by a customer on a conversation, rendered in the dashboard.
Defined locally in the conversations crate to avoid a circular dependency
with the feedback crate.

TestConfigResult.description:
Result of `POST /platform/ai/config/test` and `POST /tenant/ai/config/test`.

On success (`ok: true`) the response includes `provider`, `model`, and
`latency_ms`; on failure (`ok: false`, HTTP 422) the response includes
`error_category` and a sanitized `detail` string. The optional fields
are always absent on the opposite side of the success/failure split.

UpdateCustomerPayload.description:
Body of `PATCH /tenant/customers/{id}`.  `TriState` for nullable contact
fields distinguishes "absent" (no change) from explicit `null` (clear)
from a present value.  Identifiers and metadata use replace-the-set
semantics — they are present and become the new set.

OpenAPI note: `TriState<T>` is a Rust-only tri-state enum (no `ToSchema`
derive is emitted by utoipa 5.x for the generic case).  The contact
fields are documented as `Option<Option<String>>` — *optional and
nullable* — via field-level `value_type` overrides, which is the
faithful wire representation:
  * field omitted  → absent  → not in the JSON
  * `null`         → clear   → JSON `null`
  * `"value"`      → value   → JSON `"value"`

UpdateTenantRequest.description:
`UpdateTenantRequest` — body for `PATCH /api/v1/platform/tenants/{id}`.

Every field is typed as `Option<Option<String>>` so the handler can
distinguish three cases per the spec's absent-vs-null semantics:

  * Field absent → `None` (do not touch the column).
  * Field = `null` → `Some(None)`. For non-nullable columns (`name`,
    `slug`, `plan`, `status`) this is an explicit *invalid* value
    and produces 422. For nullable columns (`contactName`,
    `contactEmail`) it is an explicit *clear* signal.
  * Field = "x" → `Some(Some("x"))` (set the column, with validation).

`contact_name` and `contact_email` use the same three-state encoding
but the handler treats `Some(None)` and `Some(Some(""))` as a clear.

UsageDetailResponse.description:
Response envelope for `GET /tenant/ai/usage/{id}`. The handler returns
`{"data": <row>}`; the wrapper makes that contract explicit in the schema.

VerifyRequest.description: The second sign-in step: exactly one of `code` and `recoveryCode`.

code.description: A six-digit code from the authenticator app.

recoveryCode.description: One of the single-use recovery codes.

WidgetConversationData.description:
`{ "conversation": … }` wrapper required by the public widget contract
(specs/023-website-chat-widget/contracts/public-widget-api.md).

WidgetInstanceRef.description: Reference to a widget instance that originated a conversation.

info.description: REST API for the multi-tenant AI customer service platform. All authenticated endpoints require a valid `app_session` cookie.
info.title: AI Customer Service Platform API

post.description: Accepts an email + password pair, verifies them against the `users` table, and on success issues a signed JWT session. The JWT is returned to the client via a `Set-Cookie: app_session=...; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/` response header. The response body is the same profile shape returned by `GET /me` (see `tenancy::routes::MeResponse`); the typed body schema is filled in by the tenancy-module annotation pass. This endpoint is public — no `app_session` cookie is required.

200.description: Login successful. Returns the user profile and sets the `app_session` cookie.

202.description: The password was right and the user has two-factor authentication: no session yet. Sets a short-lived `app_mfa_pending` cookie; complete the sign-in with `POST /auth/mfa/verify`.

400.description: Validation failed (missing email or password).

post.description: Revokes the current session's JTI and clears the `app_session` cookie. Returns 204 No Content on success. The `Set-Cookie` response header sets `app_session=; Path=/; HttpOnly; Max-Age=0` (or an already-expired date) so clients can drop the cookie. Requires a valid `app_session` cookie; unauthenticated requests are rejected with 401.

Creates a new authenticator secret for the signed-in user and returns it once, as base32 and as an `otpauth://` URI. Needs the current password, so a stolen session alone cannot add an authenticator. The factor stays inactive until `POST /auth/mfa/enrol/confirm` proves a code. Starting again replaces an unconfirmed secret. Returns 409 when the user already has an active factor.

201.description: A secret to add to an authenticator app.

409.description: Two-factor authentication is already set up.

post.description: Checks a code from the authenticator app. On success the factor becomes active, ten recovery codes are returned once (stored only as hashes), and the `app_session` cookie is replaced by a session that records the second factor. Wrong codes count toward the lockout.

200.description: Active. The recovery codes, shown once; the session cookie is replaced.

429.description: Too many wrong codes; the factor is locked.

post.summary: Confirm two-factor authentication with a code

get.description: Whether the signed-in user has an active factor, and how many recovery codes are left. Never returns a secret or a code.

post.description: Takes an authenticator code or a recovery code, together with the `app_mfa_pending` cookie that `POST /auth/login` set. On success it starts the session (the `app_session` cookie records the second factor), clears the challenge and returns the same profile body as login. A code is accepted once; five wrong codes lock the account's second factor for fifteen minutes. The challenge lasts five minutes. Public: no `app_session` cookie is needed.

200.description: Signed in. Returns the user profile and sets the `app_session` cookie.

400.description: Neither or both of `code` and `recoveryCode`.

401.description: No valid challenge (missing, expired or already used): sign in again.

429.description: Too many attempts, or the second factor is locked.

post.summary: Complete sign-in with a second factor

post.description: Public, self-serve signup (FR-AUTH-001). Creates a new tenant (workspace) on the `trial` plan, a new user account as that tenant's Owner, and starts a session — the response body is the same `MeResponse` shape returned by `GET /me`, and the `app_session` cookie is set the same way as `POST /auth/login`. The workspace slug is derived automatically from `workspaceName` (and disambiguated on collision); it can be changed later from tenant settings. Returns 409 if the email is already registered.

201.description: Workspace and account created. Returns the user profile and sets the `app_session` cookie.

400.description: Validation failed (request body is not valid JSON).

409.description: An account with this email already exists.

post.summary: Create a workspace and its first (Owner) user

get.summary:
Liveness probe. Returns `{"status": "ok"}` with HTTP 200 while the process
is running. Used by orchestrators to decide when to restart a process.

post.description: Receives a webhook delivery for the connection identified by `token`. The body must be JSON and accompanied by an `X-Webhook-Signature: sha256=<hex>` header carrying the HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body keyed by the connection's `signing_secret`. Per-connection rate limit is 60 requests / 60 seconds; body limit is 256 KB. No authentication is required — the token in the URL is the credential. Unknown, inactive, and unverifiable deliveries all return the same generic 404 (no existence leak).

requestBody.description: Raw JSON body, HMAC-SHA256-verified before parsing

get.description: Public endpoint that returns a non-revealing preview of a pending invitation (tenant name, invitee email, role, and expiry) so the accept page can render before sign-in. Returns 404 for unknown tokens, soft-deleted or suspended tenants, and accepted/revoked invitations; returns 410 for expired invitations.

404.description: Invitation not found (or the tenant is not active).

post.description: Public endpoint that accepts a pending invitation. If the caller is signed in and the principal's email matches the invitation, a membership is created for the existing user. Otherwise an anonymous accept creates a new user account (supplying `displayName` and `password`) and signs them in via a new `app_session` cookie. Returns 404 for unknown tokens, soft-deleted or suspended tenants, and accepted/revoked invitations; returns 410 for expired or already-used tokens.

200.description: Invitation accepted. The response body is the same `MeResponse` shape returned by `GET /me`.

400.description: Validation failed (request body is not valid JSON).

422.description: Validation failed (per-field, e.g. invalid display name or password).

200.description: Current user principal and tenant membership summary. Requires an authenticated session.
